sources.publisher: Internet Engineering Task Force / RFC Editor
sources.name: RFC 9530 — Digest Fields
sources.role: HTTP content/representation integrity and digest-input contract
verified_facts: Content-Digest is calculated over actual HTTP message content, while Repr-Digest is calculated over selected representation data.
Digest fields identify the hash algorithm and encoded digest value and can be validated by a receiver for integrity.
Representation digests depend on representation metadata and can differ from content digests when range requests or content codings are involved.
semantic_limits: A valid digest proves agreement with the chosen digest input; it does not prove source authority, terrain accuracy, vertical datum or parcel containment.
Content-Digest on a partial response must not be treated as a digest of the complete source object.
Digest integrity does not provide authentication, authorization or privacy and must not create a business row by itself.

sources.publisher: Internet Engineering Task Force / RFC Editor
sources.name: RFC 8288 — Web Linking
sources.role: link context, target and relation-type contract
verified_facts: A Web link relates a context resource to a target resource through one or more relation types.
RFC 8288 defines serialization of links in the HTTP Link header field.
Relation types can be registered tokens or extension relation URIs and carry application-defined semantics.
semantic_limits: A link does not prove that its target was fetched, that the target bytes are complete or that the target is authoritative.
A relation type describes a relationship and is not a checksum, provenance receipt or measurement result.
A linked alternate, describedby or related resource must not be silently substituted for the exact distribution used for height calculation.

sources.name: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) — Version 3
sources.role: dataset/distribution, access/download URL, version and checksum metadata contract
verified_facts: DCAT distinguishes datasets from distributions and uses accessURL, accessService and downloadURL to describe access routes.
downloadURL identifies a directly downloadable file for a distribution, while media type and format describe its representation.
DCAT 3 adds version relationships and a checksum mechanism that records algorithm and checksum value for a distribution file.
semantic_limits: A landing page, access URL or download URL is metadata and does not prove that the exact bytes were downloaded and read.
A version label or current-version relation must not replace a pinned immutable distribution identity and digest.
A checksum in catalog metadata is only useful when the checksum metadata itself is obtained through a trusted independent route.

sources.name: Data on the Web Best Practices — Data Quality Vocabulary (DQV)
sources.role: quality metric, measurement, annotation, policy and provenance metadata contract
verified_facts: DQV extends DCAT with classes and properties for quality measurements, metrics, annotations, policies and certificates.
A quality measurement binds a value to the metric it measures and the dataset or distribution on which it was computed.
DQV supports provenance and third-party quality assessments rather than defining one universal meaning of quality.
semantic_limits: A quality score is metadata about a dataset or distribution and is not a parcel elevation or height-difference value.
Metric identity, computation target, date, unit and provenance must be bound before comparing quality measurements.
Publisher annotations or certificates do not replace byte-level integrity, exact geometry, vertical datum and measurement-method evidence.
